name: Rayl

open.name: Enterable surfaces
open.what: text input, select, checkbox and toggle, and the modal that holds them
open.detail: In a system with no strokes, a control that ACCEPTS input has to read as enterable through a change of ground alone. That is one decision and all four follow from it. Martijn is designing it. Until it lands there is no correct form in this system.

open.name: Semantic colour
open.what: nothing means error, warning, success or info
open.detail: Every colour in the palette sits on one hue, so any of these is the brand's first hue break. Do not draft a palette colour in to stand for a state and do not borrow a red.

open.name: Deep Black #11110F
open.what: the dark-mode ground, and the one palette colour not on the approved frame
open.detail: It ships and it works. Either it joins the palette or dark mode grounds on a colour already in it.

open.name: Hover: the ladder or the token
open.what: two approved sources give a Paper base two different hovers
open.detail: The L* ladder says Bone, five steps away. surface/idle-hover says Off White, one step. Build with the tokens — they are what ships — but the disagreement is real and wants a decision.

open.name: A container's padding
open.what: "a container pads one step below the gap it sits in"
open.detail: It held when the page ran 72 and a band padded 48. The page runs 96 now and the band still pads 48, where the rule would say 72. Do not apply it to anything new.

open.name: 96 on the spacing scale
open.what: the page rhythm is 96 and the scale as written stops at 72
open.detail: 96 steps by 12 like every other member and is what rayl-page actually uses, so it is listed. Confirm it is a member rather than a page-only figure.

open.name: The 8 radius
open.what: every control rounds 8; the board's own ladder is 4, 12, 24
open.detail: 8 is measured off the approved UI rather than the demo, and where the two disagree the UI wins. Worth confirming the ladder gains an 8.

open.name: Component states
open.detail: Hover, pressed, disabled and focus are covered by the tokens. These four are not, and a tool without them is a demo.

open.name: The Rayl look
open.what: the layered gradient treatment, and the largest single gap in the system
open.detail: Flat vector art with gradient fills, stamped repeatedly, no specular highlight — it is not lighting and cannot be reproduced with lighting. There is no reference file in this repo. Everything else here makes a build correct; this is what makes it Rayl. Say the reference is missing rather than approximating it.

open.name: The reveal button's label
open.what: White #FFFFFF on the approved frame, Off White in the ink table
open.detail: One value, two approved sources. Ask before using either.

open.name: A colour change runs 120ms
open.what: the ground under a button moves at 120ms ease-out, not on the system's curve
open.detail: Every documented movement is 280ms on cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), and the guideline says both surfaces move together on the same duration and curve. The shipped controls do not: a hover's colour change is 120ms ease-out while the label rolls at 280ms. It reads well and it is what ships, so it is written down rather than quietly corrected — but it is a second easing in a system whose whole argument is that there is one.

open.name: The fonts
open.what: Azeret and Concrette here are TRIAL cuts
open.detail: Fine for internal work and prototypes. The licensed files have to replace them before anything built with this goes public.

open.name: CMYK
open.what: the printed values are arithmetic, not a profile conversion
open.detail: Fine on screen, not fine at a printer.

note: Never write a hex in a build. Name a token; it resolves per mode.

display.role: titles and subheads, 24 and up only
display.optical size: S ships; M and XL exist

label.use: names a section, and nothing else

meaning.6: parts of one control — buttons in a cluster, a stepper's digits
meaning.12: things in a document: blocks on the page, frames in a field
meaning.24: a group led by nothing larger than a 24
meaning.36: a group led by a 36; three columns of a split
meaning.48: a group led by a 48 or a 72; two columns of a split

meaning.8: a control — button, option cell, card, swatch
meaning.24: a container — a rail, a frame, a panel
meaning.half the height: anything meant to read as fully round

stagger.what: one character to the next, compressed so a roll never runs past 400ms

press up.what: and coming back — deliberately slower than down

a line returns.what: before a swapped line goes back to what it was

Page.rayl-page: the app or panel column: ground, 72 rhythm, 520 wide
Page.rayl-page is-wide: the same at 960, for a page that has to breathe
Page.rayl-section: a section; its gap is derived the same way
Page.rayl-stack: a group; its gap is what its largest text asks for
Page.rayl-grid: an even grid of cards or swatches
Page.rayl-head: a header or footer row: mark on the left, controls right
Page.rayl-card: a panel that lifts off the ground
Page.rayl-row: a named control on one line
Page.rayl-row-name: the name in that row — 12, Medium, full ink, sentence case
Page.rayl-label: the 8 uppercase section label, and nothing else
Page.rayl-hint: a quiet line of explanation under a block
Page.rayl-gap-6: set a group's gap when it has no heading to derive one

Wide layout.rayl-hero: the opening statement of a page
Wide layout.rayl-band: a full-width band; is-ink for one in ink
Wide layout.rayl-media: a picture that follows the column beside it

Document.rayl-doc: on the body: the document ground rather than the app one
Document.rayl-chapter: an 8 label on the ground, over the blocks under it
Document.rayl-rail-foot: pinned to the floor of a rail
Document.rayl-field: the things of a block, stacked 12 apart
Document.rayl-field-row: frames side by side inside a field
Document.rayl-frame: one white box holding one thing; is-tall, is-wide
Document.rayl-frame-tag: names a frame, turned on its side, costing no height
Document.rayl-container: a plain white box for a header or footer

Controls.rayl-btn: the button; aria-pressed for on, data-icon for an icon
Controls.rayl-ibtn: the reveal button: the label contracts, a circle irises open
Controls.rayl-seg: the option group — exactly one on; is-joined, is-tight
Controls.rayl-seg-opt: one cell of it; is-on, is-third
Controls.rayl-seg-name: the name that opens a joined bar — never a disabled cell
Controls.rayl-slider: the track: data-min, data-max, data-val, data-step
Controls.rayl-line: a value on a line that rolls; data-label, data-swap
Controls.rayl-icon: an icon on its own; data-icon

Type.rayl-serif: Concrette, on a size class from 24 up

missing.a brief will ask for: any form, any name field, any numeric entry
a list too long for an option group
a setting that is on or off on its own
a confirm, an export dialog, a settings panel
the approved panel draws one — every section label carries a – and nothing implements it
a label on an icon button
more than one view in a panel
anything reporting that a background job finished
an export, an upload, a render
a count, a status, a filter
every panel taller than its frame
a control panel beside a canvas — the only layout the system cannot express
